title.zh: 卷一百七十四 列傳第六十一: 姚燧 郭貫 夾谷之奇 劉賡 耶律有尚 郝天挺 張孔孫
title.en: Volume 174 Biographies 61: Yao Sui, Guo Guan, Jia Guzhiqi, Liu Geng, Ye Luyoushang, Hao Tianting, Zhang Kongsun
title.raw: 卷一百七十四 列傳第六十一: 姚燧 郭貫 夾谷之奇 劉賡 耶律有尚 郝天挺 張孔孫 Volume 174 Biographies 61: Yao Sui, Guo Guan, Jia Guzhiqi, Liu Geng, Ye Luyoushang, Hao Tianting, Zhang Kongsun

sentences.zh: 姚燧，字端甫，世系見燧伯父樞傳。

translations.literal: Yao Sui, styled Duanfu; his lineage is set forth in the biography of Sui's paternal uncle Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Sui, styled Duanfu, came of a family whose lineage is recorded in the biography of his paternal uncle Yao Shu.

sentences.zh: 父格。

translations.literal: His father was Ge.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Ge.

sentences.zh: 燧生三歲而孤，育於伯父樞。

translations.literal: Sui lost his father at age three and was reared by his paternal uncle Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was orphaned at the age of three and was brought up by his uncle Yao Shu.

sentences.zh: 樞隱居蘇門，謂燧蒙暗，教督之甚急，燧不能堪。

translations.literal: Shu lived in retirement at Sumen, considered Sui dull and benighted, and urged and supervised his studies very strictly; Sui could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had retired to Sumen and judged the boy slow-witted; he drove his studies relentlessly, and Sui found it unbearable.

sentences.zh: 楊奐馳書止之曰：「燧，令器也，長自有成爾，何以急為！」

translations.literal: Yang Huan sent a hurried letter to stop him, saying: "Sui is fine material; when grown he will achieve maturity on his own—why be so urgent!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huan wrote in haste to dissuade him: "Sui is promising timber; in time he will mature of his own accord—why press him so hard?"

sentences.zh: 且許醮以女。

translations.literal: He also promised to betroth his daughter to him.
translations.idiomatic: He also pledged his daughter in betrothal to the boy.

sentences.zh: 年十三，見許衡於蘇門。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he met Xu Heng at Sumen.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he met Xu Heng at Sumen.

sentences.zh: 十八，始受學於長安。

translations.literal: At eighteen he first received instruction in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he began his formal studies in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時未嘗為文，視流輩所作，惟見其不如古人，則心弗是也。

translations.literal: At the time he had never yet composed essays; when he looked at what his contemporaries wrote, he saw only that it fell short of the ancients, and in his heart he disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet tried his hand at writing, but when he read what his contemporaries produced he could see only how far it fell short of the ancients, and he inwardly rejected it.

sentences.zh: 二十四，始讀韓退之文，試習為之，人謂有作者風。

translations.literal: At twenty-four he first read the writings of Han Tuizhi, tried practicing composition in that style, and people said he had the manner of a master writer.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four he first read Han Yu and tried writing in his manner; contemporaries said he already showed a master's touch.

sentences.zh: 稍就正於衡，衡亦賞其辭，且戒之曰：「弓矢為物，以待盜也；

translations.literal: He gradually sought correction from Heng; Heng also admired his literary style and admonished him, saying: "Bow and arrow are things made to await robbers;
translations.idiomatic: He gradually submitted his work to Xu Heng for correction; Heng admired his prose but warned him: "Bows and arrows exist to meet robbers;

sentences.zh: 使盜得之，亦將待人。

translations.literal: if robbers obtain them, they too will await men.
translations.idiomatic: if robbers seize them, they too will wait upon men.

sentences.zh: 文章固發聞士子之利器，然先有能一世之名，將何以應人之見役者哉！

translations.literal: Literary composition is indeed the sharp weapon by which a scholar makes his name heard, yet if one first gains a reputation able to command an age, how will one answer those who come to employ one!
translations.idiomatic: Writing is the scholar's weapon for making a name, yet if you win a reputation that fills the age, how will you answer everyone who comes to command your pen?

sentences.zh: 非其人而與之，與非其人而拒之，鈞罪也，非周身斯世之道也。」

translations.literal: To give it to one who is not the right person, and to refuse one who is not the right person—the guilt is equal; neither is the way to preserve oneself in this world."
translations.idiomatic: To grant your writing to the wrong man is as grave a fault as to refuse the right one; neither is the way to keep your footing in the world."

sentences.zh: 至元七年，衡以國子祭酒教貴冑，奏召舊弟子十二人，燧自太原驛致館下。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, Heng as Director of the Imperial Academy instructed the noble scions; he memorialized to summon twelve former disciples, and Sui came from Taiyuan by post-station relay to join them at the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270), when Xu Heng served as director of the Imperial Academy and instructed the sons of the nobility, he memorialized to recall twelve former pupils; Sui traveled by relay from Taiyuan to join them at the academy.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，仁宗居籓邸，開宮師府，燧年已七十，遣正字呂洙，如漢徵四皓故事，起燧為太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide, Renzong resided at the princely residence and opened a palace tutors' office; Sui was already seventy; he sent the proofreader Lü Zhu, following the Han precedent of summoning the Four Hoary Heads, to raise Sui as Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide (1308), while Renzong still held his princely establishment and had opened a tutors' bureau, Sui was already seventy. Renzong sent the proofreader Lü Zhu, in deliberate echo of the Han summons to the Four Greybeards, to bring Sui out of retirement as guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除承旨學士，尋拜太子少傅。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed expositor academician; soon after he was invested as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made expositor of the Hanlin Academy, and shortly thereafter was appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 武宗面諭燧，燧拜辭，謝曰：「昔臣先伯父樞嘗除是官，尚不敢拜，臣何敢受！」

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong instructed Sui in person; Sui bowed and declined, saying in thanks: "Formerly my late paternal uncle Shu was once appointed to this office and still did not dare accept the investiture—how dare I receive it!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong addressed him in person, but Sui bowed and declined, saying: "My late uncle Shu was once offered this same post and even he did not dare accept the seal—how could I?"

sentences.zh: 明年，授榮祿大夫、翰林學士承旨、知制誥兼修國史。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Hanlin Academician Expositor, Controller of Imperial Edicts, and concurrent Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with appointments as expositor of the Hanlin Academy, controller of imperial edicts, and concurrent compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 四年，得告南歸，中書以承旨召；

translations.literal: In the fourth year he obtained leave to return south; the Central Secretariat summoned him as expositor;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he obtained leave and returned south; the Central Secretariat summoned him back as expositor;

sentences.zh: 明年，復召。

translations.literal: the next year he was summoned again.
translations.idiomatic: the next year he was summoned again.

sentences.zh: 燧以病，俱不赴。

translations.literal: Sui pleaded illness and on both occasions did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Both times Sui pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 卒於家，年七十六。

translations.literal: He died at home, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 燧先在蘇門山時，讀《通鑑綱目》，嘗病國統散於逐年，不能一覽而得其離合之概，至告病江東，著《國統離合表》若干卷，年經而國緯之，如《史記》諸《表》，將附硃熹《凡例》之後，復取徽、建​​二本校仇，得三誤焉，序於《表》首。

translations.literal: While Sui was earlier on Mount Sumen he read the Comprehensive Mirror in Outline and once lamented that dynastic legitimacy was scattered year by year, so that one could not grasp at a glance the general pattern of separation and reunion; when he took sick leave in Jiangdong he composed several fascicles of Tables of the Separation and Reunion of Dynastic Legitimacy, threading years vertically and states horizontally, like the tables in the Records of the Grand Historian, intending to append them after Zhu Xi's General Principles; he then collated the Huizhou and Jian editions and found three errors, which he set forth in a preface at the head of the tables.
translations.idiomatic: During his years on Mount Sumen, Sui read Zhu Xi's Comprehensive Mirror in Outline and was troubled that legitimacy was dispersed year by year, so that one could not see at a glance how states split and reunited. When he retired sick to the lower Yangzi region he wrote several fascicles of Tables of the Separation and Reunion of Dynastic Legitimacy, arranging years down the page and states across, in the manner of the Shiji tables, intending to append them after Zhu Xi's General Principles. He then collated the Huizhou and Jian editions and found three errors, which he explained in a preface to the work.

sentences.zh: 略曰：「其一，建安二十五年，徽本作『延康元年』。

translations.literal: In summary he said: "First: in the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an, the Huizhou edition reads 'first year of Yan'kang.
translations.idiomatic: In brief he wrote: "First: for the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an the Huizhou edition gives 'first year of Yan'kang.

sentences.zh: 《凡例》：中歲改元，在興廢存亡之際，以前為正。

translations.literal: The General Principles state: when the reign title is changed mid-year, at the juncture of rise, fall, survival, and extinction, the earlier designation is taken as correct.
translations.idiomatic: The General Principles hold that when a reign title changes mid-year, at the moment of a dynasty's rise or fall the earlier designation should stand.

sentences.zh: 當從建本，於建安二十五年下，注『改元延康』。

translations.literal: One should follow the Jian edition and under the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an add the note 'changed reign title to Yan'kang.'
translations.idiomatic: The Jian edition is correct: under the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an one should note 'reign title changed to Yan'kang.'

sentences.zh: 其二，章武三年，徽本大書『三年，後主禪建興元年』，建本無『三年』，則昭烈為無終。

translations.literal: Second: in the third year of Zhangwu the Huizhou edition writes in large characters 'third year; the Later Lord abdicates, first year of Jianxing,' whereas the Jian edition lacks 'third year,' which would make the Latter Lord have no end.
translations.idiomatic: Second: for the third year of Zhangwu the Huizhou edition heads the year 'third year; the Later Lord abdicates, first year of Jianxing,' but the Jian edition omits 'third year,' as though the Latter Lord's reign had no proper conclusion.

sentences.zh: 徽、建皆曰『後主』，於君臣父子之教，所害甚大，是起十四卷、盡十六卷，凡曰後主者，皆失於刊正也。

translations.literal: Both Huizhou and Jian call him 'Later Lord,' which greatly harms the teaching of ruler and minister, father and son; from the opening of fascicle fourteen through the end of fascicle sixteen, wherever 'Later Lord' appears, all are errors of editorial correction.
translations.idiomatic: Both editions call him 'Later Lord,' a grave injury to the moral order of ruler and subject, father and son. From fascicle fourteen through sixteen, every instance of 'Later Lord' is a failure of editorial judgment.

sentences.zh: 當於三年下注『帝禪建興元年』，明年大書『帝禪建興二年』，庶前後無齟齬也。

translations.literal: One should under the third year add the note 'the Emperor abdicates, first year of Jianxing,' and the next year write in large characters 'the Emperor abdicates, second year of Jianxing,' so that before and after there is no contradiction.
translations.idiomatic: Under the third year one should note 'the Emperor abdicates, first year of Jianxing,' and the following year head the entry 'the Emperor abdicates, second year of Jianxing,' so that the sequence is internally consistent.

sentences.zh: 其三，天寶十五載注『肅宗皇帝至德元載』，明年惟曰『二載』，為無始。

translations.literal: Third: in the fifteenth year of Tianbao a note reads 'Emperor Suzong, first year of Zhide'; the next year says only 'second year,' as though it had no beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the fifteenth year of Tianbao carries a note 'Emperor Suzong, first year of Zhide,' but the next year is headed only 'second year,' as if the new reign had no proper beginning.

sentences.zh: 當大書『二載』上加『肅宗皇帝至德』，使上同於開元。

translations.literal: One should write in large characters above 'second year' 'Emperor Suzong, Zhide,' so that it matches above with Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The second year should be headed 'Emperor Suzong, Zhide, second year,' matching the treatment given earlier reigns such as Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 三者鈞失，而建安之取，至德之去，統固在也。

translations.literal: All three errors are equal faults, yet in adopting Jian'an and removing Zhide, the thread of legitimacy remains intact.
translations.idiomatic: All three are editorial lapses, yet in preferring the Jian'an reading and correcting the Zhide entry the thread of dynastic legitimacy remains sound.

sentences.zh: 若章武之距建興，才三年耳，遽有帝父主子之異，豈不於統大有關乎！」

translations.literal: If from Zhangwu to Jianxing is only three years, yet suddenly there is the difference between emperor and father, lord and son—does this not bear greatly upon legitimacy!"
translations.idiomatic: From Zhangwu to Jianxing is a mere three years, yet suddenly father becomes emperor and son becomes subject—is this not a matter of the highest consequence for legitimacy!"

sentences.zh: 詳見《序篇》。

translations.literal: The details are given in the preface.
translations.idiomatic: The full argument appears in the preface.

sentences.zh: 燧之學，有得於許衡，由窮理致知，反躬實踐，為世名儒。

translations.literal: Sui's learning owed something to Xu Heng; through investigating principle to achieve knowledge and turning back upon himself in earnest practice, he became a renowned Confucian of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's learning owed much to Xu Heng: he pursued principle to knowledge and tested it in his own conduct, and was accounted one of the age's leading Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 為文閎肆該洽，豪而不宕，剛而不厲，舂容盛大，有西漢風，宋末弊習，為之一變。

translations.literal: In composition his style was broad, expansive, and comprehensive; bold without excess, forceful without harshness, measured and grand, with the manner of the Western Han; the decadent habits of late Song were thereby transformed.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was broad and comprehensive, bold without extravagance, forceful without harshness, measured and ample, with the air of Western Han writing; he did much to break the bad habits of late Song letters.

sentences.zh: 蓋自延祐以前，文章大匠，莫能先之。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, before the Yanyou era no master of letters could rank ahead of him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Yanyou period (1314–1320), no writer of note could be placed above him.

sentences.zh: 或謂世無知燧者，曰：「豈惟知之，讀而能句，句而得其意者，猶寡。」

translations.literal: Some said the age did not know Sui; he replied: "It is not only that they know him—those who can read and parse his sentences, and parsing grasp his meaning, are still few."
translations.idiomatic: When someone said the world did not appreciate Sui, he answered: "They may know my name, but how few can read my sentences, parse them, and grasp their meaning."

sentences.zh: 燧曰：「世固有厭空桑而思聞鼓缶者乎，然文章以道輕重，道以文章輕重。

translations.literal: Sui said: "Surely in the world there are those who tire of the empty mulberry yet long to hear the beating of earthen jars; yet writing is weighed by the Way, and the Way is weighed by writing.
translations.idiomatic: Sui said: "There are always men who tire of plain fare yet crave coarse music; but writing is judged by the Way, and the Way is judged by writing.

sentences.zh: 彼復有班孟堅者出，表古今人物，九品中必以一等置歐陽子，則為去聖賢也有級而不遠，其文雖無謝、尹之知，不害於行後。

translations.literal: If again a Ban Menjian should appear, tabulating men ancient and modern, he would surely place Master Ouyang in the first rank of the nine grades; then though removed from the sages and worthies, there would be degrees yet not great distance; though his writing lacked the discernment of Xie and Yin, it would not harm his standing among posterity.
translations.idiomatic: If another Ban Gu should compile a roster of men through the ages, he would surely place Master Ouyang in the top grade; though that sets him below the sages, the distance would not be vast, and though his prose lacked admirers like Xie and Yin, it would not keep him from a place among the great writers of later ages.

sentences.zh: 豈有一言幾乎古，而不聞之將來乎！」

translations.literal: How could there be a single word approaching the ancients that would not be heard in the future!"
translations.idiomatic: Can a line that nearly equals the ancients fail to reach posterity?"

sentences.zh: 當時孝子順孫，欲發揮其先德，必得燧文始可傳信；

translations.literal: At the time filial sons and obedient grandsons who wished to set forth the virtue of their forebears had to obtain Sui's writing before it could be transmitted as credible;
translations.idiomatic: In his day no dutiful son or grandson who wished to celebrate a forebear's virtue could do so credibly without a text from Sui;

sentences.zh: 其不得者，每為愧恥。

translations.literal: those who could not obtain it were each time shamed.
translations.idiomatic: and those who failed to secure one often felt ashamed.

sentences.zh: 故三十年間，國朝名臣世勳、顯行盛德，皆燧所書。

translations.literal: Therefore for thirty years the renowned ministers, hereditary merit-holders, and eminent deeds and great virtue of the dynasty were all written by Sui.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years the memorial inscriptions for the dynasty's great ministers, hereditary nobles, and men of outstanding conduct were almost all from his hand.

sentences.zh: 每來謁文，必其行業可嘉，然後許可，辭無溢美。

translations.literal: Whenever anyone came to request a text, their conduct and achievement had to be praiseworthy before he would consent; his wording had no excess of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted commissions only when the subject's conduct deserved praise, and he never lavished empty compliment.

sentences.zh: 又稍廣置燕樂，燧則為之喜而援筆大書，否則弗易得也。

translations.literal: Moreover, if they somewhat expanded the banquet music, Sui would be pleased and take up the brush to write at length; otherwise his writing was not easily obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If they laid on a generous feast with music, he would be pleased and write freely; otherwise his brush was hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 時高麗瀋陽王父子，連姻帝室，傾貲結朝臣。

translations.literal: At the time the king of Korea, the Prince of Shenyang, father and son, were allied by marriage to the imperial house and poured out wealth to bind court officials.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Korea, the Prince of Shenyang, and his son were then allied to the imperial house by marriage and spent lavishly to win over courtiers.

sentences.zh: 一日，欲求燧詩文，燧靳不與，至奉旨，乃與之。

translations.literal: One day they sought Sui's poetry and prose; Sui was stingy and would not give them; only when an imperial order was received did he comply.
translations.idiomatic: One day they asked for his poetry and prose; he refused until an imperial edict compelled him to comply.

sentences.zh: 王贈謝幣帛、金玉、名畫五十篚，盛陳致燧。

translations.literal: The prince sent gifts of thanks—silks, gold and jade, and famous paintings, fifty baskets—displayed in full array and presented to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent fifty baskets of silk, gold and jade, and famous paintings as thanks, laid out in full display before Sui.

sentences.zh: 燧即分散諸屬官及史胥侍從，止留金銀，付翰林院為公用器皿，燧一無所取。

translations.literal: Sui at once distributed them among his subordinate officials, clerks, and attendants; he kept only the gold and silver and turned it over to the Hanlin Academy as communal vessels; Sui took nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sui immediately distributed the gifts among his staff and attendants, kept only the gold and silver for the Hanlin Academy's common use, and took nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 人問之，燧曰：「彼籓邦小國，唯以貨利為重，吾能輕之，使知大朝不以是為意」。

translations.literal: When people asked him, Sui said: "That vassal state is a small country that values profit alone; I can treat it lightly and let them know the great court does not regard such things as important."
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, he said: "That petty vassal kingdom cares only for gain; by treating their gifts lightly I show them the great court sets no store by such things."

sentences.zh: 其器識豪邁過人類如此。

translations.literal: His breadth of vision and bold spirit surpassing others were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: In breadth of mind and bold spirit he surpassed ordinary men in just this way.

sentences.zh: 然頗恃才，輕視趙孟頫、元明善輩，故君子以是少之。

translations.literal: Yet he rather relied on his talent and looked down on Zhao Mengfu, Yuan Mingshan, and their like; therefore gentlemen held this against him somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was rather proud of his gifts and looked down on Zhao Mengfu, Yuan Mingshan, and others, for which thoughtful men held him somewhat less in esteem.

sentences.zh: 平生所著，有《牧庵文集》五十卷行於世。

translations.literal: Throughout his life his writings included the Muan Collected Works in fifty fascicles, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, the Muan wenji in fifty fascicles, circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子三：塤，圻，城。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Xun, Qi, and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Xun, Qi, and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 郭貫，字安道，保定人。

translations.literal: Guo Guan, styled Andao, was a man of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Guan, styled Andao, was a native of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 以才行見推擇，為樞密中書掾，調南康路經歷，擢廣西道提刑按察司判官，會例格，授濟南路經歷。

translations.literal: Recommended and selected for ability and conduct, he served as a clerk in the Secretariat of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was transferred to administrator of Nankang Circuit, was promoted to investigating censor and surveillance commissioner of Guangxi Circuit, and when regulations barred further promotion was appointed administrator of Jinan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for ability and integrity, he served as a clerk in the Secretariat of the Bureau of Military Affairs, became administrator of Nankang Circuit, was promoted investigating censor of Guangxi, and when regulations blocked further advancement was appointed administrator of Jinan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 至元二十七年，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Zhiyuan he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Zhiyuan (1290) he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 承詔分江北沿淮草地，劾淮西宣慰使昂吉兒父子專權，久不遷調，蠹政害民。

translations.literal: By imperial order he partitioned the pasturelands along the Huai in northern Jiang, and impeached Angi'er, pacification commissioner of Huai West, father and son, for monopolizing power, long remaining without transfer, corrupting government and harming the people.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he surveyed pasturelands along the Huai in the north and impeached Angi'er, pacification commissioner of Huai West, and his son for monopolizing office, refusing rotation, and corrupting government to the people's harm.

sentences.zh: 三十年，僉湖南肅政廉訪司事。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed vice commissioner of the Hunan Commission for Government Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1293) he became vice commissioner of the Hunan Commission for Government Integrity.

sentences.zh: 大德初，遷湖北道，言「今四省軍馬，以數万計，徵八百媳婦國，深入為炎瘴萬里不毛之地，無益於國。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dade he was transferred to Hubei Circuit and said: "Today the armies of the four provinces number in the tens of thousands; campaigning against the Kingdom of Eight Hundred Wives, penetrating deep into a region of miasma and fever, ten thousand li of barren land, brings no benefit to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dade era (1297–1307) he was transferred to Hubei and memorialized: "The four provinces now field armies numbering in the tens of thousands for a campaign against the Kingdom of Eight Hundred Wives—a march deep into malarial wastes a thousand li across that brings the state no benefit."

sentences.zh: 五年，遷江西道，賑恤饑民，有惠政，入為御史臺都事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Jiangxi Circuit, relieved and comforted famine victims, had benevolent policies, and entered the capital as director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was moved to Jiangxi, where he relieved famine victims with effective charity, then was recalled to the capital as director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷集賢待制，進翰林直學士，奉詔與遼陽行省平章政事別速台徹里帖木兒往鎮高麗。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to attendant at the Hall of Gathered Worthies, advanced to direct academician of the Hanlin, and by imperial order went with Biesutai Cheremutemur, regional councilor of Liaoyang, to garrison Korea.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became attendant at the Hall of Gathered Worthies and was promoted direct academician of the Hanlin; by imperial order he accompanied Biesutai Cheremutemur, regional councilor of Liaoyang, to oversee Korea.

sentences.zh: 十一年，召為河東廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned as vice commissioner of the Hedong Commission for Government Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was recalled as vice commissioner of the Hedong Commission for Government Integrity.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，仁宗至五台山，貫進見，仁宗因問：「廉訪使滅里吉歹何以有善政？」

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide Renzong came to Mount Wutai; Guan presented himself for audience, and Renzong thereupon asked: "How did the integrity commissioner Mielijitai achieve good government?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide (1309) Renzong visited Mount Wutai; Guo Guan was presented to him, and Renzong asked: "How did the integrity commissioner Mielijitai win a reputation for good government?"

sentences.zh: 左右對曰：「皆副使郭貫之教也。」

translations.literal: Those at his side answered: "It is all the instruction of Vice Commissioner Guo Guan."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants replied: "It was all the teaching of Vice Commissioner Guo Guan."

sentences.zh: 因賜貫瑪瑙數珠、金織文幣，入為吏部考功郎，遂拜治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed on Guan agate prayer beads and gold-woven patterned silks; Guan entered the capital as director of merit evaluation in the Ministry of Personnel, and was then appointed supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong then gave Guo agate prayer beads and gold-woven silks, recalled him to the capital as director of merit evaluation in the Ministry of Personnel, and soon appointed him supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 四年，除禮部尚書，帝親書其官階曰嘉議大夫，以授有司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Minister of Rites; the Emperor personally wrote his official rank as Grand Master for Discussion and gave it to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Minister of Rites; the emperor personally wrote his rank as Grand Master for Discussion and handed the document to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，擢淮西廉訪使，尋留不遣，改侍御史，俄遷翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was promoted integrity commissioner of Huai West; soon he was detained and not sent, was changed to attendant censor, and shortly was transferred to Hanlin attendant expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing (1312) he was promoted integrity commissioner of Huai West but was kept at court, made attendant censor, and soon Hanlin attendant expositor.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為淮西廉訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as integrity commissioner of Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent out as integrity commissioner of Huai West.

sentences.zh: 建言「宜置常平倉，考校各路農事」。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Constant-level granaries should be established and agriculture in each circuit examined."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed establishing ever-normal granaries and reviewing agricultural conditions in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，召拜中書參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou he was summoned and appointed associate administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanyou (1315) he was summoned as associate administrator of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，升左丞，加集賢大學士。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted left chancellor and given the additional title of grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted left chancellor and made grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 五年，除太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 貫​​言：「皇太子受金寶已三年，宜行冊禮；

translations.literal: Guan said: "The crown prince has received the golden seal and treasure for three years; the investiture ceremony should be performed;
translations.idiomatic: Guan said: "The crown prince has held the golden seal for three years; it is time to perform the investiture rites;

sentences.zh: 又，輔導之官，早宜選置。」

translations.literal: moreover, the officials who tutor and guide him should early be selected and appointed."
translations.idiomatic: and the tutors who will guide him should be chosen without delay."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His advice was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 六年，加太子賓客，謁告還家。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given the additional title of guest of the Heir Apparent and, requesting leave, returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made guest of the heir apparent, obtained leave, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，復起為集賢大學士，尋致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi he was again raised as grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, and soon retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi (1321) he was recalled as grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies but soon retired.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，遷翰林學士承旨，不起。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was transferred to Hanlin Academician Expositor but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiding (1324) he was offered expositor of the Hanlin Academy but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，以疾卒，年八十有二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun he died of illness, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhishun (1331) he died of illness at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿大夫、河南行省平章政事、柱國，追封蔡國公，諡文憲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, regional councilor of Henan, and Pillar of the State; was enfeoffed as Duke of Cai and given the posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, regional councilor of Henan, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Cai, and given the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 貫​​博學，精於篆籀，當世冊寶碑額，多出其手云。

translations.literal: Guan was broadly learned and skilled in seal and archaic script; the edicts, treasures, and stele inscriptions of the age mostly came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was broadly learned and a master of seal and archaic script; most of the age's imperial edicts, regalia inscriptions, and stele headings were said to be his work.

sentences.zh: 夾谷之奇

translations.literal: Jia Guzhiqi
translations.idiomatic: Jia Guzhiqi

sentences.zh: 夾谷之奇，字士常，其先出女真加古部，後訛為夾谷，由馬紀嶺撒曷水徙家於滕州。

translations.literal: Jia Guzhiqi, styled Shichang, was descended from the Jurchen Jiagu tribe, later corrupted to Jiagu; from Majiling on the Sahe River the family moved their residence to Tengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Guzhiqi, styled Shichang, came of the Jurchen Jiagu clan, later written as Jiagu; his forebears moved from Majiling on the Sahe River to settle in Tengzhou.

sentences.zh: 之奇少孤，舅杜氏攜之至東平，因受業於康曄。

translations.literal: Zhiqi was orphaned young; his maternal uncle the Du clan brought him to Dongping, where he received instruction from Kang Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was taken by his uncle's family to Dongping, where he studied under Kang Ye.

sentences.zh: 授濟寧教授，辟中書省掾。

translations.literal: He was appointed professor at Jining and was recruited as a clerk of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as professor at Jining and was recruited as a clerk in the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大兵南伐宋，授行省左右司都事。

translations.literal: When the great army marched south to attack Song, he was appointed director of the left and right bureaus of the regional secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the great southern campaign against Song he was appointed director of the left and right bureaus of the regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時行省官與中書權臣有隙，特遣使核其財用，而之奇職文書，亦被按問。

translations.literal: At the time the regional secretariat officials had a rift with powerful ministers of the Central Secretariat; an envoy was specially dispatched to audit their finances, and Zhiqi, whose duty was documents, was also investigated.
translations.idiomatic: The regional secretariat was then at odds with powerful ministers at court, and a special envoy was sent to audit its accounts; Zhiqi, who handled its documents, was investigated as well.

sentences.zh: 張弘範率其屬詣使者言：「夾谷都事素公清，若少有侵漁，弘範當與連坐。」

translations.literal: Zhang Hongfan led his subordinates to the envoy and said: "Director Jiagu has always been upright and clean; if he has taken the slightest in private gain, Hongfan should share the punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongfan went with his staff to the envoy and said: "Director Jia has always been scrupulously honest; if he has taken so much as a penny in graft, I ask to share his punishment."

sentences.zh: 會御史臺立，擢之奇僉江南浙西道提刑按察司事，既而移僉江北淮東。

translations.literal: When the Censorate was established he was promoted vice commissioner of the Jiangnan and Zhexi Circuit Commission for Investigation and Censorship, and later was transferred vice commissioner of Jiangbei and Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Censorate was established he was made vice commissioner of the Jiangnan and Zhexi investigating commission, and later transferred to Jiangbei and Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，召為吏部郎中，立陟降澄汰之法，著為令式。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan he was summoned as director in the Ministry of Personnel, established methods for promotion, demotion, clarification, and elimination, and set them down as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan (1282) he was recalled as a director in the Ministry of Personnel, drew up rules for promotion, demotion, and removal of unfit officials, and codified them as standing regulations.

sentences.zh: 歲大旱，有司議平穀價，以遏騰湧之患。

translations.literal: In a year of great drought the responsible offices debated stabilizing grain prices to check the harm of soaring prices.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought officials proposed fixing grain prices to curb runaway inflation.

sentences.zh: 之奇言：「莫若省經費，輟土木之役，庶足召和氣，弭災變，而有豐稔之期。」

translations.literal: Zhiqi said: "Better to reduce expenditures and suspend construction projects; then perhaps one may summon harmonious qi, quell calamities, and have the prospect of abundant harvest."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqi said: "Better to cut state spending and halt construction projects; that may restore harmony, end the calamity, and bring a good harvest in due course."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遷左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to left supporter of goodness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1284) he was made left supporter of goodness.

sentences.zh: 時裕宗為皇太子，每進見，必賜坐，顧遇甚優。

translations.literal: At the time the Latter Lord was crown prince; whenever Zhiqi came for audience he was always granted a seat and treated with exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Chengzong was then heir apparent; whenever Zhiqi attended audience he was given a seat and treated with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 權臣有欲以均輸法益國賦者，慮提刑按察司撓其事，請令與轉運司並為一職，詔集群臣議之。

translations.literal: A powerful minister wished to use the equalizing transport law to increase state revenue and, fearing the investigating censorate would obstruct the matter, requested that it be merged with the transport commission into one office; an edict summoned the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful minister wished to revive the equalizing transport system to swell state revenue and, fearing the investigating censors would block him, proposed merging them with the transport commission; the emperor ordered a full ministerial debate.

sentences.zh: 之奇言：「按察司者，控制諸路，發擿姦伏，責任匪輕。

translations.literal: Zhiqi said: "The investigating censorate controls the circuits, exposes hidden wrongdoing, and bears no light responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqi said: "The investigating censorate oversees the circuits, uncovers hidden crime, and bears a weighty charge.

sentences.zh: 若使理財，則心勞事冗，將彌縫自救之不暇，又安能繩糾他人哉！

translations.literal: If made to manage finances, the mind would be weary and affairs numerous; one would have no leisure to patch and save oneself—how could one bind and correct others!
translations.idiomatic: If they were made to handle revenue as well, they would be too busy covering their own tracks to discipline anyone else!

sentences.zh: 併之弗便。」

translations.literal: Merging the offices was not convenient."
translations.idiomatic: The merger was rejected as impractical."

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 又與諭德李謙條具時政十事，上之皇太子：一曰正心，二曰睦親，三曰崇儉，四曰幾諫，五曰戢兵，六曰親賢，七曰革敝，八曰尚文，九曰定律，十曰正名。

translations.literal: He also, together with preceptor Li Qian, itemized ten matters of current policy and presented them to the crown prince: first, rectifying the mind; second, harmonizing kin; third, honoring frugality; fourth, subtle remonstrance; fifth, curbing arms; sixth, drawing near the worthy; seventh, reforming abuses; eighth, esteeming letters; ninth, fixing laws; tenth, correcting names.
translations.idiomatic: With the preceptor Li Qian he also drew up ten points on current policy for the crown prince: rectify the mind; harmonize kin; honor frugality; remonstrate subtly; curb military excess; draw near the worthy; reform abuses; esteem learning; fix the laws; and correct names.

sentences.zh: 會皇太子薨，除翰林直學士，改吏部侍郎，遂拜侍御史。

translations.literal: When the crown prince died he was appointed direct academician of the Hanlin, was changed to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and was then invested as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince died he was made direct academician of the Hanlin, then vice minister of personnel, and soon attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，丁母憂，以吏部尚書起復，屢請終制，不許。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he mourned his mother; he was recalled from mourning as Minister of Personnel, repeatedly requested to complete the full mourning period, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he entered mourning for his mother; recalled as Minister of Personnel before the mourning term ended, he repeatedly asked to complete the full period of filial observance but was refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died.

sentences.zh: 之奇慮識精審，明於大體，而不忽細微，為政卓卓可稱，雖老於吏學者，自以為不及。

translations.literal: Zhiqi's reflection and discernment were precise and careful; he was clear about the larger pattern yet did not neglect minute matters; in government his achievements were outstanding and praiseworthy—even veterans of administrative studies considered themselves his inferiors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqi thought with precision, grasped the larger pattern without neglecting detail, and governed with marked distinction; even seasoned administrators admitted they could not match him.

sentences.zh: 為文章尤簡嚴有法，多傳於世云。

translations.literal: In literary composition he was especially concise, strict, and methodical, and much of his work circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was especially concise and disciplined, and much of it has survived.

sentences.zh: 劉賡，字熙載，洺水人。

translations.literal: Liu Geng, styled Xizai, was a man of Moshui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Geng, styled Xizai, was a native of Moshui.

sentences.zh: 五世祖逸，以郡吏治獄，有陰德。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Yi, as a commandery clerk who handled legal cases, had hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Yi, while serving as a commandery clerk in charge of legal cases, performed hidden acts of merit.

sentences.zh: 祖肅，為左三部尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Su was Minister of the Left Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Su served as Minister of the Left Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 賡幼有文名，師事翰林學士王磐。

translations.literal: Geng had a literary reputation from youth and took as his teacher the Hanlin academician Wang Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Geng won a literary reputation early and studied under the Hanlin academician Wang Pan.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，用薦者授國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, on recommendation he was appointed compiler at the National History Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan (1276) he was recommended and appointed a compiler at the National History Office.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to attendant for Hanlin documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became attendant for Hanlin documents.

sentences.zh: 辟為司徒府長史，仍兼應奉。

translations.literal: He was recruited as chief steward of the Minister of Education's office while still holding the attendant post concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as chief steward of the Minister of Education's office while retaining his Hanlin attendant post.

sentences.zh: 補外，同知德州事，考滿，擢太廟署丞、太常博士，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He filled an outside post as vice administrator of Dezhou; when his term assessment was complete he was promoted director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Office and erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Posted outside the capital as vice administrator of Dezhou, he completed his term assessment and was promoted director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Office and erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 是時，御史中丞崔彧好盛氣待人，他御史拜謁，或平受之，獨見賡，則待以上客。

translations.literal: At the time the censor-in-chief Cui Yu liked to treat others with overbearing airs; when other censors came to pay respects he sometimes received them on equal terms, but when he saw Geng he treated him as an honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief Cui Yu was overbearing toward his colleagues; when other censors called on him he often received them as equals, but he treated Geng as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，升翰林直學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade he was promoted direct academician of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dade (1298) he was promoted direct academician of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 六年，奉使宣撫陝西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was sent on a mission to pacify and comfort Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was dispatched on a pacification mission to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 由侍講學士升學士。

translations.literal: From attendant expositor he was promoted academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Hanlin attendant expositor to academician.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，遷禮部尚書，仍兼翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was transferred to Minister of Rites while still holding the Hanlin academician post concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide (1309) he was made Minister of Rites while retaining his Hanlin academician post.

sentences.zh: 尋拜侍御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 頃之，還翰林為學士承旨，兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Shortly he returned to the Hanlin as expositor academician and concurrently Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to the Hanlin as expositor and was made concurrent director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 國學故事，伴讀生以次出補吏，莫不爭先出。

translations.literal: By the established practice of the Imperial Academy, companion readers were released in order to fill official posts, and none failed to vie to go out first.
translations.idiomatic: By academy custom, companion readers were released in seniority order to take official posts, and all competed to leave first.

sentences.zh: 時有一生，親老且貧，同舍生有名在前者，因博士以告曰：「我齒頗少，請讓之先。」

translations.literal: At the time there was one student whose parents were old and poor; a dormitory mate whose name ranked ahead, through the erudite, reported: "I am rather junior in standing—please let him go first."
translations.idiomatic: One student had aged, impoverished parents; a classmate whose name ranked above his asked the erudite: "I am junior in standing—please let him go out before me."

sentences.zh: 賡曰：「讓，德之恭也。」

translations.literal: Geng said: "Yielding is the reverence of virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Geng said: "Yielding is the reverence of virtue."

sentences.zh: 從其讓，別為書薦其人，朝廷反先用之。

translations.literal: He granted the yielding, separately wrote a letter recommending the man who had yielded, and the court in fact employed him first.
translations.idiomatic: He approved the request, wrote a separate recommendation for the student who had yielded, and the court in fact appointed him first.

sentences.zh: 自是六館之士，皆知讓之為美德也。

translations.literal: From this time the students of the six halls all knew yielding as a beautiful virtue.
translations.idiomatic: From then on students in all six halls understood yielding as a virtue.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，遷集賢大學士，仍兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was transferred to grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while still holding the Imperial Academy directorship concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing (1312) he became grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while remaining director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，復為承旨；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was again made expositor;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou (1314) he was again made expositor;

sentences.zh: 六年，拜太子賓客；

translations.literal: in the sixth year he was appointed guest of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth year he was made guest of the heir apparent;

sentences.zh: 七年，復入集賢為大學士；

translations.literal: in the seventh year he again entered the Hall of Gathered Worthies as grand academician;
translations.idiomatic: in the seventh year he returned to the Hall of Gathered Worthies as grand academician;

sentences.zh: 尋又入翰林為承旨。

translations.literal: soon he again entered the Hanlin as expositor.
translations.idiomatic: and soon after was again expositor of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was given the additional rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiding (1324) he was given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 會集議上尊號，賡獨抗言其不可，事遂已。

translations.literal: When there was a joint deliberation on bestowing an honorific title, Geng alone spoke out in opposition that it should not be done, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated granting an honorific title, Geng alone protested that it should not be done, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianli (1328) he died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 賡久典文翰，當時大製作多出其手，以耆年宿德，為朝廷所推重云。

translations.literal: Geng long presided over literary documents; the great compositions of the time mostly came from his hand; as an elder of advanced years and established virtue, he was esteemed and relied upon by the court.
translations.idiomatic: Geng long directed the literary offices, and most of the age's major state compositions came from his hand; as an elder of established reputation, he was greatly esteemed at court.

sentences.zh: 耶律有尚

translations.literal: Ye Luyoushang
translations.idiomatic: Ye Luyoushang

sentences.zh: 耶律有尚，字伯強，遼東丹王十世孫。

translations.literal: Ye Luyoushang, styled Boqiang, was a tenth-generation descendant of the Liao Prince of Eastern Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Luyoushang, styled Boqiang, was a tenth-generation descendant of the Liao Prince of Eastern Dan.

sentences.zh: 祖父在金世嘗官於東平，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather in the Jin era had once held office at Dongping and thereupon made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had served in Dongping under the Jin and settled his family there.

sentences.zh: 有尚資識絕人，篤志於學，受業許衡之門，號稱高第弟子。

translations.literal: Youshang's native ability surpassed others; he devoted himself ardently to learning, received instruction in Xu Heng's school, and was acclaimed a leading disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Youshang's gifts were extraordinary; he devoted himself to learning under Xu Heng and was accounted one of his foremost pupils.

sentences.zh: 其學邃於性理，而尤以誠為本，儀容辭令，動中規矩，識與不識，莫不服其為有道之君子。

translations.literal: His learning was profound in the principles of human nature, yet he especially took sincerity as his root; in bearing, speech, and deportment his every movement accorded with rule; whether known to him or not, none failed to submit that he was a gentleman possessed of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: His learning ran deep in Neo-Confucian principle, with sincerity as its foundation; in bearing and speech he never departed from propriety, and all who met him, whether friend or stranger, acknowledged him as a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，衡罷中書左丞，除集賢大學士，兼國子祭酒，以教國人之子弟，乃奏以門人十二人為齋長以伴讀，有尚其一也。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan Heng was dismissed as left assistant minister of the Central Secretariat, appointed grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and concurrent Director of the Imperial Academy to instruct the sons of the state's people; he memorialized that twelve of his disciples serve as hall chiefs as companion readers—Youshang was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan (1271) Xu Heng left the post of left assistant minister and became grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and director of the Imperial Academy to instruct the sons of the nobility. He memorialized that twelve disciples serve as hall chiefs and companion readers; Youshang was among them.

sentences.zh: 十年，衡告免還鄉里，朝廷乃以有尚等為助教，嗣領其學事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Heng requested leave and returned to his home district; the court then appointed Youshang and others as assistant instructors to succeed him in directing academic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Xu Heng retired to his home district, and the court appointed Youshang and others assistant instructors to carry on his teaching.

sentences.zh: 居久之，拜監察御史，不赴。

translations.literal: After he had been in the post a long time he was appointed investigating censor but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was appointed investigating censor but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 除秘書監丞，出知薊州，為政以寬簡得民情。

translations.literal: He was appointed assistant director of the Palace Library, went out as prefect of Jizhou, and in government won the people's hearts through leniency and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: He was made assistant director of the Palace Library, then prefect of Jizhou, where lenient and straightforward government won the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 裕宗在東宮，召為詹事院長史。

translations.literal: When the Latter Lord was in the Eastern Palace he was summoned as chief steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Chengzong was heir apparent, Youshang was summoned as chief steward of the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 自有尚既去，而國學事頗廢，廷議以謂非有尚無足以繼衡者，除國子司業。

translations.literal: After Youshang had left, academic affairs at the Imperial Academy fell somewhat into neglect; court deliberation held that without Youshang no one was fit to succeed Heng, and he was appointed vice director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After his departure academy affairs declined, and the court concluded that only Youshang could succeed Xu Heng; he was appointed vice director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 時學館未建，師弟子皆寓居民屋，有尚屢以為言。

translations.literal: At the time the academy buildings had not yet been erected; teachers and students all lodged in private houses, and Youshang repeatedly spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: The academy buildings had not yet been built, and teachers and students lodged in private houses; Youshang repeatedly urged that this be remedied.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，朝廷乃大起學舍，始立國子監，立監官，而增廣弟子員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the court greatly raised academy buildings, first established the Imperial Academy Directorate, appointed directorate officials, and expanded the number of disciples.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (1287) the court built new academy halls, established the Imperial Academy directorate, appointed its officers, and increased the number of students.

sentences.zh: 於是有尚升國子祭酒，儒風為之丕振。

translations.literal: Thereupon Youshang was promoted Director of the Imperial Academy, and Confucian teaching was thereby greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Youshang was then promoted director of the academy, and Confucian learning flourished anew under his leadership.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以親老，辭職歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, because his parents were aged, he resigned his post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1290) he resigned and returned home to care for his aged parents.

sentences.zh: 大德改元，復召為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title to Dade he was again summoned as Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dade era began (1297) he was recalled as director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 尋除集賢學士，兼其職。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while holding that post concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while retaining the directorship.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷太常卿，又遷集賢學士。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then again transferred to academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he became Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then returned to the Hall of Gathered Worthies as academician.

sentences.zh: 八年，葬父還鄉里。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he buried his father and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he buried his father and returned home.

sentences.zh: 已而朝廷思用老儒，以安車召之於家，累辭不允，復起為昭文館大學士，兼國子祭酒，階中奉大夫。

translations.literal: Before long the court wished to employ an aged Confucian; with a comfort carriage he was summoned from his home; he repeatedly declined but was not permitted; he was again raised as grand academician of the Hall of Brilliant Literature, concurrent Director of the Imperial Academy, with the rank of Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The court then wished to employ a venerable scholar and sent a comfort carriage to summon him from home. He declined repeatedly but was overruled, and was restored as grand academician of the Hall of Brilliant Literature and concurrent director of the Imperial Academy, with the rank of Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 有尚前後五居國學，其立​​教以義理為本，而省察必真切；

translations.literal: Youshang five times in all presided over the Imperial Academy; in establishing teaching he took principle and reason as the foundation, and in self-examination he was always earnest and true;
translations.idiomatic: Youshang headed the Imperial Academy on five separate occasions. He grounded instruction in moral principle and demanded genuine self-examination;

sentences.zh: 以恭敬為先，而踐履必端愨。

translations.literal: he put reverence first, and in practice was always upright and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: he put reverence first and insisted on upright conduct in practice.

sentences.zh: 凡文詞之小技，綴緝雕刻，足以破裂聖人之大道者，皆屏黜之。

translations.literal: All petty skills of literary phrasing, patchwork ornament and carving that could rupture the great Way of the sages, he banished and rejected.
translations.idiomatic: He barred ornamental literary tricks that could fracture the sages' great Way.

sentences.zh: 是以諸生知趨正學，崇正道，以經術為尊，以躬行為務，悉為成德達材之士。

translations.literal: Therefore the students knew to pursue correct learning, honor the correct Way, esteem classical studies, and take personal practice as their task; all became men of completed virtue and realized talent.
translations.idiomatic: His students therefore pursued orthodox learning, honored the true Way, esteemed the classics, and took practice as their task, and all became men of completed virtue and realized ability.

sentences.zh: 大抵其教法一遵衡之舊，而勤謹有加焉。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, his teaching method followed Heng's former practice, with added diligence and care.
translations.idiomatic: His method followed Xu Heng's precedent, with even greater diligence.

sentences.zh: 身為學者師表者數十年，海內宗之，猶如昔之宗衡也。

translations.literal: For decades he personally served as the model teacher of scholars; within the seas he was revered, just as in former times Heng had been revered.
translations.idiomatic: For decades he was the model teacher of scholars throughout the realm, revered as Xu Heng had once been.

sentences.zh: 有尚既以年老，力請還家，朝廷复頒楮幣七千緡，即其家賜之。

translations.literal: When Youshang, on account of advanced age, strongly requested to return home, the court again issued seven thousand strings of paper currency and bestowed it at his home.
translations.idiomatic: When age compelled him to retire, the court sent seven thousand strings of paper currency to his home as a parting gift.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十六，賜諡文正。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-six and was granted the posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-six and was given the posthumous title Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 郝天挺

translations.literal: Hao Tianting
translations.idiomatic: Hao Tianting

sentences.zh: 郝天挺，字繼先，出於朵魯別族，自曾祖而上，居安肅州。

translations.literal: Hao Tianting, styled Jixian, came from the Dorben tribe; from his great-grandfather upward the family resided in Ansu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Tianting, styled Jixian, came of the Dorben tribe; from his great-grandfather's generation the family lived in Ansu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父和上拔都魯，太宗、憲宗之世多著武功，為河東行省五路軍民萬戶。

translations.literal: His father Heshang Badulu in the eras of Taizong and Xianzong achieved many military feats and served as commander of military and civilian households of the five circuits of the Hedong regional secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Heshang Badulu won distinction in the campaigns of Taizong and Xianzong and served as commander of military and civilian households for the five circuits of the Hedong regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天挺英爽剛直，有志略，受業於遺山元好問，以勳臣子，世祖召見，嘉其容止，有旨：宜任以政，俾執文字，備宿衛春宮。

translations.literal: Tianting was bright, forthright, and upright, with ambition and strategy; he received instruction from Yishan Yuan Haowen; as the son of a meritorious minister he was summoned for audience by Shizu, who admired his bearing and deportment; an edict stated that he should be entrusted with government, made to handle documents, and assigned to guard the Eastern Palace on night duty.
translations.idiomatic: Tianting was brilliant, forthright, and ambitious; he studied under Yuan Haowen of Yishan. As the son of a meritorious minister he was summoned by Kublai, who admired his bearing and ordered that he be trained for government service, handle documents, and serve on night guard at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 裕宗遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: The Latter Lord treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Chengzong treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 建省雲南，選官屬，遂除參議雲南行尚書省事，尋升參知政事，又擢陝西漢中道廉訪使。

translations.literal: When Yunnan Province was established and officials were selected, he was appointed deliberator of the Yunnan Regional Secretariat, soon promoted associate administrator, and then elevated integrity commissioner of Shaanxi and Hanzhong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan province was established he was chosen as deliberator of its regional secretariat, soon promoted associate administrator, and then integrity commissioner of Shaanxi and Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為吏部尚書，尋除陝西行御史臺中丞，又遷四川行省參政及江浙行省左丞，俱不赴。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the capital as Minister of Personnel, soon was appointed censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Regional Censorate, and was again transferred to associate administrator of Sichuan and left chancellor of Jiang-Zhe regional secretariats—all of which he did not take up.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered the capital as Minister of Personnel, then censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Regional Censorate, and was offered posts as associate administrator of Sichuan and left chancellor of Jiang-Zhe—all of which he declined.

sentences.zh: 拜中書左丞，與宰相論事，有不合，輒面斥之。

translations.literal: He was appointed left chancellor of the Central Secretariat; when he discussed affairs with the chief minister and there was disagreement, he would at once rebuke him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted appointment as left chancellor of the Central Secretariat and, when he disagreed with the chief minister on policy, rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 一日，以奏事敷陳明允，特賜黃金百兩，不受。

translations.literal: One day, because in memorializing affairs he set forth clear and fair arguments, he was specially granted one hundred taels of gold, which he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: One day, after he presented a particularly clear and forceful memorial, the emperor granted him a hundred taels of gold, which he refused.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非利汝也，第旌汝肯言耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This is not to enrich you; it is only to honor your willingness to speak out."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "This is not for your profit; it is only to honor your willingness to speak frankly."

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，仁宗以太后命，首定大難，及武宗還自朔方，遂入正大統，定策之際，天挺與有力焉。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong by the Empress Dowager's command first settled the great crisis; when Wuzong returned from the northern frontier he then entered and rectified the succession; at the time of deciding policy Tianting exerted strong influence.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, Renzong, acting on the empress dowager's orders, first resolved the succession crisis; when Wuzong returned from the north the legitimate line was restored, and Tianting played a decisive part in the deliberations.

sentences.zh: 仁宗臨御，收召故老天挺與少保張閭等十人，共議大政，革尚書省之弊，遂成皇慶之治。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne he recalled the aged Tianting together with Junior Guardian Zhang Lü and nine others—ten men in all—to deliberate on great affairs, reform the abuses of the Secretariat, and thereby achieve the governance of Huangqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne he recalled the aged Tianting with Junior Guardian Zhang Lü and eight others—ten men in all—to deliberate on great affairs, reform the abuses of the Secretariat, and bring about the good government of the Huangqing era.

sentences.zh: 又出為江西、河南二省右丞，召拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: He again went out as right chancellor of Jiangxi and Henan provinces, and was summoned and appointed censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as right chancellor of Jiangxi and Henan and was recalled as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 入見，首陳紀綱之要，以獵為喻曰：「御史職在擊姦，猶鷹揚焉，禽之，弱者易獲也，其力大者，必借人力。

translations.literal: On entering audience he first set forth the essentials of law and discipline, using the hunt as a metaphor: "The censor's duty is to strike at wrongdoing, like the hawk soaring; when it seizes its quarry, the weak are easily taken, but the strong require human aid.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he first explained the essentials of discipline, using the hunt as a metaphor: "The censor's duty is to strike at wrongdoing, like a hawk on the wing. Weak prey are easily taken; powerful quarry requires human assistance.

sentences.zh: 不然，不惟失其前禽，仍或有傷鷹之患矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise one not only loses the quarry before one, but may also have the harm of injuring the hawk."
translations.idiomatic: Without it one not only loses the quarry but may wound the hawk itself."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其言，既出，台臣皆以為賀，風紀大振。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his words; when he came out, the censorate officials all regarded it as cause for congratulation, and disciplinary standards were greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his words. When he left the audience, his colleagues congratulated him, and censorial discipline was greatly revived.

sentences.zh: 又上疏陳七事，曰惜名爵、抑浮費、止括田、久任使、論好事、獎農務本、勵學養士，詔中書省舉行之。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial setting forth seven matters: cherishing titles and emoluments, curbing extravagant expenditures, stopping land surveys for confiscation, long tenure in office, judging meritorious undertakings, rewarding agriculture and honoring the fundamental, and encouraging learning and nurturing scholars; an edict ordered the Central Secretariat to implement them.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized seven reforms: cherish titles and salaries, curb extravagance, halt confiscatory land surveys, lengthen terms of office, scrutinize meritorious projects, reward agriculture as the foundation of the state, and encourage learning and nurture scholars. The court ordered the Central Secretariat to carry them out.

sentences.zh: 尋俾均逸於外，拜河南行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted equitable rest in the provinces and appointed regional councilor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent to the provinces for a period of rest and appointed regional councilor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時河南王卜憐吉歹為丞相，待以師禮，由是政化大行。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Henan, Bulqanjadai, served as chancellor and treated him with the rites due a teacher; thereby government and transformation were greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Henan, Bulqanjadai, then served as chancellor and treated him as a teacher; under their joint administration good government flourished.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangqing he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangqing (1313) he died at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿大夫、中書平章政事、柱國，追封冀國公，諡文定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, regional councilor of the Central Secretariat, and Pillar of the State; was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji and given the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, regional councilor of the Central Secretariat, and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, and given the posthumous title Wending.

sentences.zh: 天挺嘗修《雲南實錄》五卷，又注唐人《鼓吹集》一十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Tianting once compiled five fascicles of the Veritable Records of Yunnan and also annotated the Tang Drum-and-Pipe Collection in ten fascicles, both of which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Tianting compiled five fascicles of the Veritable Records of Yunnan and annotated the Tang Drum-and-Pipe Collection in ten fascicles; both works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子佑，字君輔，小字朵魯別台。

translations.literal: His son You, styled Junfu, had the childhood name Dorbentai.
translations.idiomatic: His son You, styled Junfu, was known in childhood as Dorbentai.

sentences.zh: 由宿衛補官，仁宗時拜殿中侍御史，以廉直著名，大受知遇。

translations.literal: Through palace guard service he received an official appointment; in Renzong's time he was appointed palace attendant censor, was famed for integrity and uprightness, and received great favor and trust.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through the palace guard and, under Renzong, was appointed palace attendant censor, winning renown for integrity and receiving the emperor's strong favor.

sentences.zh: 遷陝西行省參知政事，拜陝西行御史臺侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to associate administrator of the Shaanxi regional secretariat and appointed attendant censor of the Shaanxi Regional Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted associate administrator of the Shaanxi regional secretariat and appointed attendant censor of the Shaanxi Regional Censorate.

sentences.zh: 張孔孫

translations.literal: Zhang Kongsun
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kongsun

sentences.zh: 張孔孫，字夢符，其先出遼之烏若部，為金人所並，遂遷隆安。

translations.literal: Zhang Kongsun, styled Mengfu, was descended from the Wuru tribe of Liao; when it was absorbed by the Jin people the family moved to Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kongsun, styled Mengfu, came of the Wuru tribe of Liao; when the Jin absorbed their territory the family moved to Long'an.

sentences.zh: 父之純，為東平萬戶府參議，夜夢謁孔子廟，得賜嘉果，已而孔孫生，因丐名於衍聖公，遂名今名。

translations.literal: His father Zhichun served as deliberator of the Dongping Myriarch Office; one night he dreamed of visiting the Temple of Confucius and receiving fine fruit as a gift; shortly afterward Kongsun was born, and he therefore begged a name from the Duke Who Continues the Sage, who gave him his present name.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhichun served as deliberator of the Dongping Myriarch Office. One night he dreamed of visiting the Temple of Confucius and receiving fine fruit; when Kongsun was born shortly afterward, he asked the Duke Who Continues the Sage for a name, and received the name Kongsun.

sentences.zh: 既長，以文學名，辟萬戶府議事官，萬戶嚴忠範之兄為陝西行省平章政事，聘孔孫，以母老不應。

translations.literal: When grown he was famed for letters and learning and was recruited as deliberating officer of the Myriarch Office; the elder brother of Myriarch Yan Zhongfan served as regional councilor of Shaanxi and invited Kongsun, but because his mother was aged he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he won a literary reputation and was recruited as deliberating officer of the Myriarch Office. The elder brother of Myriarch Yan Zhongfan, then regional councilor of Shaanxi, invited him to serve, but he declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 時汴梁既下，太常樂師流寓東平，舊章缺落，止存登歌一章而已。

translations.literal: At the time Bianliang had already fallen; Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians were scattered and lodged at Dongping; the old regulations were lost, and only the ascending song in one section remained.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Bianliang, Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians had taken refuge at Dongping; most of the old ritual music was lost, and only one ascending hymn survived.

sentences.zh: 世祖居潛邸，嘗召樂師至日月山觀之，至是，徐世隆奏帝，宜增設宮縣及文、武二舞，以備大典。

translations.literal: When Shizu resided at the princely establishment he once summoned the musicians to Sun-Moon Mountain to observe them; at this time Xu Shilong memorialized the Emperor that palace bells and chimes and the civil and military dances should be added to complete the great ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai still held his princely establishment he had summoned the musicians to Sun-Moon Mountain for inspection. Xu Shilong now memorialized that palace bells and chimes and the civil and military dances should be restored for the great state ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 因詔徐世隆為太常卿，而孔孫以奉禮郎為之副，以董樂師，肄成，獻之京師。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon appointed Xu Shilong Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Kongsun as his deputy in the post of ceremonial officer, to supervise the musicians; when practice was complete they presented the result in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xu Shilong Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Kongsun his deputy as ceremonial officer to supervise the musicians. When their work was complete they presented the restored music in the capital.

sentences.zh: 廉希憲居政府，辟為掾。

translations.literal: When Lian Xixian held office in the government he recruited Kongsun as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Lian Xixian held power in the government he recruited Kongsun as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 及安童為相，尤禮重之，授戶部員外郎，出為南京總管府判官。

translations.literal: When An'tong became chancellor he especially honored and esteemed him, appointed him vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, and sent him out as judge of the Nanjing Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When An'tong became chancellor he treated Kongsun with special respect, appointed him vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, and sent him out as judge of the Nanjing Metropolitan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時方議下襄樊，朝廷急用兵，孔孫謂：「今以越境私販坐罪者，動以千數，宜開自新之條，俾得效戰贖死。」

translations.literal: At the time there was deliberation on reducing Xiang and Fan; the court urgently needed troops; Kongsun said: "Today those convicted for smuggling across borders number in the thousands; a clause for self-renewal should be opened so they may serve in battle to redeem death."
translations.idiomatic: As the court debated the reduction of Xiangyang and Fancheng and urgently needed troops, Kongsun said: "Thousands are now imprisoned for cross-border smuggling. Open a path to repentance and let them redeem their lives by serving in battle."

sentences.zh: 朝論采之。

translations.literal: Court opinion adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 僉四川道提刑按察司事，尋升湖北道提刑按察副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Sichuan Circuit Commission for Investigation and Censorship, and soon was promoted vice commissioner of the Hubei Circuit Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner of the Sichuan investigating commission and soon promoted vice commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 行部巴陵，有囚三百人，因怒龔乙建言興銀利，發其墳墓而燒其家，燒死者三人。

translations.literal: When he conducted his tour at Baling there were three hundred prisoners who, in anger at Gong Yi's proposal to revive silver profits, had opened his grave and burned his house, and three died in the fire.
translations.idiomatic: On circuit at Baling he found three hundred prisoners who, enraged by Gong Yi's proposal to revive silver mining, had desecrated his grave and burned his house, killing three people in the blaze.

sentences.zh: 有司以真圖財殺人坐之，孔孫原其情，減罪。

translations.literal: The responsible offices charged them with murder for true gain; Kongsun excused their circumstances and reduced the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Officials had charged them with murder for gain; Kongsun took account of their motives and reduced the sentences.

sentences.zh: 遷浙西提刑按察副使，改同知保定路總管府事，俄拜侍御史，行御史臺事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Zhexi investigating commission, was changed to vice administrator of the Baoding Metropolitan Prefecture, and soon was appointed attendant censor and directed censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Zhexi, made vice administrator of Baoding Metropolitan Prefecture, and soon appointed attendant censor with charge of censorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 至元二十二年，安童復入相，言於帝曰：「阿合馬顓政十年，親故迎合者，往往驟進，據顯位；

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhiyuan An'tong again entered the chancellorship and said to the Emperor: "Ahmad monopolized government for ten years; kinsmen and friends who flattered him often rose suddenly and held eminent posts;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Zhiyuan (1285) An'tong returned to the chancellorship and told the emperor: "For ten years Ahmad monopolized power; his kin and flatterers rose overnight to high office;

sentences.zh: 獨劉宣、張孔孫二人，恬守故常，終始如一。」

translations.literal: only Liu Xuan and Zhang Kongsun, two men, calmly kept to their former ways, the same from beginning to end."
translations.idiomatic: only Liu Xuan and Zhang Kongsun remained unchanged from first to last."

sentences.zh: 乃除宣吏部尚書，孔孫禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuan was appointed Minister of Personnel and Kongsun Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was then made Minister of Personnel and Kongsun Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋升孔孫禮部尚書，擢燕南提刑按察使。

translations.literal: Soon Kongsun was promoted Minister of Rites and elevated investigating commissioner of Yannan.
translations.idiomatic: Kongsun was soon promoted Minister of Rites and made investigating commissioner of Yannan.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，提刑按察司改肅政廉訪司，仍為使，蒞治於大名，一以所沒贓糴粟五千斛賑饑民。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Commission for Investigation and Censorship was changed to the Commission for Government Integrity; he remained commissioner, administered at Daming, and with confiscated illicit grain purchased five thousand hu of grain to relieve famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1291) the investigating commission became the Commission for Government Integrity; he remained commissioner at Daming and used confiscated illicit funds to buy five thousand hu of grain for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 拜僉河南江北行中書省事。

translations.literal: He was appointed associate administrator of the Henan and Jiangbei Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate administrator of the Henan and Jiangbei Regional Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 亡何，除大名路總管，兼府尹，大興學校。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed metropolitan prefect of Daming Circuit, concurrently prefect, and greatly promoted schools.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made metropolitan prefect of Daming, also serving as prefect, and greatly expanded the schools.

sentences.zh: 有獻故河堤三百餘里於太后者，即上章，謂宜悉還細民，從之。

translations.literal: When someone presented more than three hundred li of former river embankments to the Empress Dowager, he at once submitted a memorial stating that all should be returned to the common people, and this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: When someone presented more than three hundred li of former river embankments to the empress dowager, he memorialized that they should all be returned to the common people, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 擢淮東道肅政廉訪司使，因讞獄鹽場，民尹執中兄弟誣伏為強盜，平反之。
